question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the District Planning Committee?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 243-ZD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 243-ZD of the Indian Constitution mandates the establishment of a District Planning Committee (DPC) in every state at the district level.
 
• The primary function of the DPC is to consolidate the plans prepared by the Panchayats and Municipalities in the district and to prepare a draft development plan for the district as a whole.
 
• The DPC is required to consider matters of common interest between the Panchayats and the Municipalities, including spatial planning, sharing of water and other physical and natural resources, integrated development of infrastructure, and environmental conservation.
 
• The composition of the DPC and the manner of electing members to such committees are to be prescribed by the legislature of the state.
 
• Not less than four-fifths of the members of the DPC are to be elected by the elected members of the Panchayat at the district level and the Municipalities in the district from amongst themselves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)**

 
 
• PRIs are the rural local self-government institutions in India.
 
• They operate at three levels: Gram Panchayat (village level), Panchayat Samiti (block level), and Zilla Parishad (district level).
 
• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 provided constitutional status to the PRIs.
 
• PRIs aim to promote decentralized governance, ensuring greater participation of people in decision-making processes.
 
 
 
• **Municipalities**
 
 
• Municipalities are urban local self-government institutions.
 
• They are responsible for providing basic amenities and civic services to urban areas.
 
• The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 provided constitutional status to municipalities.
 
• There are different types of municipalities: Municipal Corporations, Municipal Councils, and Nagar Panchayats, depending on the size and population of the urban area.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendments Related to Local Governance**
 
 
• The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts were passed in 1992 to strengthen and empower local self-governments in rural and urban areas, respectively.
 
• These amendments introduced Articles 243 to 243-O (for PRIs) and Articles 243-P to 243-ZG (for Municipalities) in the Indian Constitution.
 
• They also mandated the creation of State Election Commissions to conduct elections to local bodies.
 
• The amendments aimed to ensure the participation of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women in local governance through reservation of seats.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Development Planning**
 
 
• Integrated development planning involves the coordinated efforts of various government agencies and local bodies to achieve balanced and sustainable development.
 
• It takes into account economic, social, environmental, and physical aspects of development.
 
• District Planning Committees play a crucial role in integrated development planning by consolidating plans from different local bodies within the district.
 
• This approach aims to address disparities and promote equitable development across different regions.
